audit_notes: Shear-lag model of one lamella loaded at its edge by the accumulated fouling drag N0 = tau_f * L_patch = 100*0.05 = 5 N/m. Interlayer stiffness k = G_i/h_i = 1e5/5e-6 = 2e10 N/m3; film stiffness E t = 1e6*2e-5 = 20 N/m; decay length 1/lambda = sqrt(E t / k) = 31.6 um; domain 300 um = 9.5 decay lengths (far-field BC valid). Analytical: u(0) = N0/(E t lambda) = 7.9e-6 m, peak interlayer shear tau_i = k u(0) = N0 lambda = 1.58e5 Pa. Fracture criterion (steady-state lap-shear energy release rate) G = N0^2/(2 E t) = 25/40 = 0.63 J/m2 > Gc = 0.5 J/m2 -> the fouled lamella sheds. Critical force for shedding N_c = sqrt(2 E t Gc) = 4.5 N/m. The window is narrow: a CLEAN lamella at service speed carries 50 Pa over the same segment length -> N = 2.5 N/m, G = 0.16 J/m2 (safe), but at 20 kn (tau ~85 Pa) or with segments longer than ~9 cm, clean lamellae also shed (G scales with (tau L)^2). Segmentation lines (perforations) every few cm are therefore mandatory, and the threshold is sensitive to speed by a factor 4 per doubling of shear. Material consumption: each shedding releases ~20 um of silicone = ~20 g/m2; a 150 um laminate gives ~7 sheddings. Released flakes are silicone microplastic (not toxic in the biocide sense, but a release into the sea). The flow drag of the clean surface equals a smooth FR coating, so no drag gain can be computed against a clean baseline: baseline_parameters left empty (gain n/a). Metric: peak interlayer shear stress at the lamella edge, informational. Dimensionless: lambda*L_domain = 9.5; G/Gc = 1.25 (fouled), 0.31 (clean).

independent_var.label: Normalised distance from lamella edge x/L

hard_constraints: clean-surface energy release rate < interlayer toughness at max service speed

baseline_description: none (no sensible conventional baseline for a shedding stress; drag equals clean FR)
